title: CSI243: the word-to-Haskell dictionary
intro: Lab and exam questions describe a function in dense wording. This table turns the phrases that come up most into what they mean and what you write.

method.title: Find the verbs, and what each one is really asking for
method.text: Underline every instruction verb, such as "write", "changes", "returns" or "using", and match each to a Haskell construct in the dictionary below. Ignore adjectives and scene-setting for now.

method.title: Rewrite the whole question as one or two short, plain sentences
method.text: If your plain-English rewrite is longer than the original, you have not decoded it yet. A correct decoding is almost always shorter than the original, because formal phrasing repeats structure ("using the function X" after already naming X) that plain English drops.

method.title: Turn the plain sentence into a signature, then the signature into equations
method.text: Only once you can say what the function does in one plain sentence should you write `funcName :: InputType -> OutputType`. The signature falls out of the plain sentence almost mechanically. See [Cheat Sheet 1](/docs/sem3/csi243/04-making-choices/cheat-sheet) for the placeholder vocabulary this step reuses.

dictionary.write: The right-hand side of `=`, or the type after the last `->`
A parameter in the signature and in the equation
`otherwise` in a guard, or the final pattern or `else` branch

dictionary.says: "for every element ...", "changes a given list using ..."
dictionary.means: Apply one function to each element, keeping the list's length
dictionary.write: `map` (Chapter 7), or a comprehension with no filter

dictionary.means: Built from a base case and a recursive case, not a Prelude shortcut

dictionary.says: "using the in-built function(s) X and Y"
dictionary.means: Compose two existing functions; do not hand-write their logic

dictionary.write: A tuple in the return type and the return expression

dictionary.means: A precondition: it decides guard order, not just guard presence
dictionary.write: The condition guarding that case must be checked before any guard whose body assumes it
`[expr | x <- xs]`, optionally with `, condition` clauses

dictionary.says: "assume the items can be arranged in some order"
dictionary.means: The element type needs `Ord`, not just any type

dictionary.says: "for any type that ...", or a constraint before `=>`
dictionary.means: Every value of that type variable must support the named operation
dictionary.write: `ClassName a =>` before the rest of the signature
